setup.why: known ids from pool (project PR-2005 / 379335744) — same dataset already confirmed by sibling probe to hold 50 options

notes:
Row count: page 1 returned 30 rows, info={page:1,page_size:30,count:50,prev:null,next:2} — confirms the same 50-option dataset the sibling probe found. Structural contract matched exactly: no drift.

1) Container shape: this capability declares response.data as a BARE ARRAY of option rows (sibling of `info`, both siblings of `success` — i.e. {success, data:[...], info:{...}}), and that is exactly what it returned: `data` is a flat array of 30 row objects, `info` is a sibling object with page/page_size/count/prev/next all present as declared. No nesting, no undeclared wrapper — unlike get_custom_field_dataset_v2, whose declared `data.options` (bare array) actually returns an object with the real array buried at `data.options.data` plus an undocumented `info` block. This capability's declared and actual shapes agree.

2) Row shape: this capability's rows are {id, option_value, is_default, colour, parent_option_id} (children present only when a parent_option_id triggers a tree rebuild — not triggered here, all null). I did not re-fetch get_custom_field_dataset_v2 in this probe, so I can't diff its actual row JSON keys byte-for-byte from here, but per that capability's own contract (as relayed for this comparison) its embedded rows are the same underlying dataset-option records; the sibling's finding described a container mismatch, not a row-shape mismatch, and the row count/ids context (50 options, 30 on page 1) lines up exactly between the two, consistent with both surfacing the same rows. Treat point 2 as UNVERIFIED at the row-field level rather than confirmed identical — would need a live side-by-side to state key names are byte-identical.

3) Pagination block: YES, declared here. `info` with {page, page_size, count, prev, next} is in this capability's declared 200 schema as a required top-level field, and `paginated:true` / `max_page_size:30` are stated in the capability metadata — the opposite of get_custom_field_dataset_v2, where the same info block was reported as returned but undeclared. This is the capability where pagination is a first-class, documented part of the contract.

4) Preference signal: neither capability's contract (this one's guidance/intent, nor what's known of the sibling's) states which to prefer when both exist for the same dataset. This capability's own guidance is suggestive though not a direct comparison statement: "This is where option ids come from. The dataset read returns options only when asked and without a stable contract; this call always returns them with their ids." That reads as an implicit steer toward this capability over get_custom_field_dataset_v2's fetch_options path for any consumer that needs option ids or a stable/paginated contract — but it never names the other capability directly, so it falls short of an explicit 'prefer this' statement.
